title: dtwiz 101 — Assessment
description: Check that you can set up dtwiz, read its analysis, deploy the Dynatrace Operator with it and troubleshoot what fails.
imagine: A customer asks you to get their Kubernetes cluster into Dynatrace with dtwiz, today.
yourGoal: Answer five questions about authentication, detection, the install and troubleshooting.

story.introduction: dtwiz analyzes a system and installs the Dynatrace ingestion method that fits it.
story.context: Every answer is in the eight steps you just completed.

questions.title: What does dtwiz status prove?
questions.content: dtwiz status shows ✓ valid on the Platform Token line.

options.text: The tenant answered one DQL query made with the token
options.explanation: Correct. dtwiz validates with fetch dt.system.events; other scopes are tested only by the calls that need them.

options.text: The token has every scope dtwiz install needs
options.explanation: No. Only the scope of the validation query is checked.

options.text: The token is a dt0s16 string
options.explanation: dtwiz calls the tenant; a format check alone would not print valid.

options.text: The Operator can already use the token
options.explanation: The Operator is not involved in status.

questions.explanation: dtwiz validates the token with one DQL query. A missing scope for a later call shows up only at that call.

questions.title: How does dtwiz find a Kubernetes cluster?
questions.content: dtwiz analyze reports Kubernetes: <none> on a machine that can reach two clusters.

options.text: Through the current kubeconfig context only
options.explanation: Correct. No current context, no Kubernetes.

options.text: By scanning the network for API servers
options.explanation: dtwiz does not scan.

options.text: Through the tenant's Kubernetes entities
options.explanation: analyze sends nothing to the tenant.

options.text: Through running Docker containers
options.explanation: Docker is reported separately.

questions.explanation: dtwiz reads the current kubeconfig context. Select the cluster with kubectl config use-context first.

questions.title: Which credential does the Operator run on after dtwiz install kubernetes?
questions.content: You need to size the platform token for a customer's install.

options.text: The same platform token, written into the DynaKube Secret as apiToken and dataIngestToken
options.explanation: Correct. So its scopes must cover the Operator, ActiveGate and log module too.

options.text: A separate operator token dtwiz mints
options.explanation: dtwiz mints nothing.

options.text: The cluster's service account
options.explanation: That is how the Operator talks to Kubernetes, not to Dynatrace.

options.text: A classic dt0c01 token
options.explanation: Only if you pass --access-token explicitly.

questions.explanation: dtwiz writes its own platform token into the Secret twice.

questions.title: Why did one pod stay in ContainerCreating on k3d?
questions.content: dtwiz install kubernetes timed out with one pod not Ready.

options.text: KSPM's node-config-collector mounts host paths that a k3d container node does not have
options.explanation: Correct. Removing spec.kspm lets the Operator delete it.

options.text: The platform token lacked an ingest scope
options.explanation: A missing scope does not stop a volume mount.

options.text: The ActiveGate image could not be pulled
options.explanation: The event named a hostPath mount.

options.text: dtwiz applied the DynaKube to the wrong namespace
options.explanation: Every pod was in dynatrace.

questions.explanation: KSPM benchmarks the node's host file system. On k3d the node is a container, so the mount fails.

questions.title: Why run checkClusterInDynatrace against a cluster that does not exist?
questions.content: Your assertion passed on the first try.

options.text: To prove the assertion can fail, so its pass really comes from your cluster
options.explanation: Correct. A DQL filter that matches nothing is not an error.

options.text: To clean up other learners' clusters
options.explanation: The check only reads.

options.text: To warm up the dtctl cache
options.explanation: There is no such cache.

options.text: Because dtctl needs two queries to authenticate
options.explanation: It does not.

questions.explanation: An assertion never seen failing proves nothing. A filter matching nothing returns zero rows without error.

learningObjectives: Install dtwiz and validate a platform token
Size a platform token for dtwiz install kubernetes
Diagnose a pod that never becomes Ready
Prove data in a shared tenant with a negative control
